note: Each fault is a hand-authored edit applied to a known-good fixture. Every 'find' must match exactly once. Classes name the contract row or requirement the fault is intended to violate; whether the independent core actually witnesses it is recorded only by a run.
authorship: Authored for Countertrace by the project owner's coding assistant; not externally reviewed.

faults.summary: A write while full is not ignored: it overwrites the oldest unread word.
faults.intended_consequence: An accepted item is lost; the next read returns a newer word.

faults.summary: A simultaneous read and write while full accepts both (full-capacity exchange).
faults.intended_consequence: The queue keeps a word the contract says to ignore.

faults.summary: A read while empty consumes a simultaneous write by bypassing it to dout.
faults.intended_consequence: A word that should remain queued is consumed in the same cycle.

faults.summary: Reset clears the read pointer and count but not the write pointer.
faults.intended_consequence: After a reset, reads return stale storage instead of newly written words.

faults.summary: A read-only operation does not decrement the occupancy count.
faults.intended_consequence: The FIFO reports items that were already removed.

faults.summary: The read pointer wraps to slot 1 instead of slot 0.
faults.intended_consequence: Words are returned out of order after the read pointer wraps.

faults.summary: Replaces count != DEPTH with count < DEPTH. Intended to be behaviorally equivalent on reachable states.
faults.intended_consequence: None expected; included so the audit reports equivalent mutants separately.

faults.summary: full asserts at DEPTH-1 words, losing one slot of capacity.
faults.intended_consequence: A legal write is refused and full is reported early.

faults.summary: The read pointer increments only its index bits, so its wrap bit never toggles.
faults.intended_consequence: After the read pointer wraps, empty and full are wrong.

faults.summary: A simultaneous read and write between empty and full outputs the head without removing it.
faults.intended_consequence: The same word is read twice.
